subject: Aurum MAP: econ validation, prefetch & batching gating

Subject: MAP kickoff + econ checks (tokens/$, prefetch, batching)

Sean —

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier. Procurement wants the Mutual Action Plan and a succinct cost sanity check before we route to finance. We need:
- a short MAP with milestones to close (SOW, SOC2 evidence, final pricing)
- an evaluation plan (pilot traffic profile, acceptance KPIs)
- a clear token-per-$ estimate with assumptions on caching/prefetch/batching so our unit-econ model can be reviewed by finance.

Attached is our initial SOW template and a CSV with simulated peak traffic (prefetch-sim-results.csv). Can your team confirm a tokens-per-inference assumption and an expected tokens/$ range for the pilot (50k DAU simulated)? We are sensitive to peak latency — any batching that risks 300ms p50 will be tricky.

Can we lock a short sync early next week? Goal is to have MAP + eval plan signed by 12/07 so procurement can begin paperwork.

Thanks,
Liam
Liam Connors
Head of Platform Integrations
Aurum Health

Liam — thanks for the clear asks and the CSV. High level plan and next steps below: 

1) MAP draft: we will send a one-page MAP (milestones + owners) by EOD 12/02. That MAP will include: pilot traffic window, acceptance KPIs, SOW sign-off, SOC2 evidence delivery, and procurement docs.

2) Eval plan: our Solutions team will run a 2-week pilot using your provided traffic profile. Acceptance criteria: functional parity, p50 latency under 250ms for 95% of calls, and no more than 2% regression in model quality on the evaluation set you provide.

3) Econ / tokens per $: karthik will share a concise assumption set (tokens per call, batching factor, cache hit rate) plus a tokens-per-dollar sensitivity table. We’ll call out a conservative and an optimistic scenario for planning.

4) Call: propose Wed 12/03 10:00am PT for a 30-minute sync to go over MAP and econ assumptions. Please confirm.

I added Karthik for the technical assumptions and Ben/Hannah to help expedite procurement and SOW language.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

Attachment: none

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>
To: Liam Connors <liam.connors@aurumhealth.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.example>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.example, hannah_schmitt@redwood.example
Date: 2026-12-02T08:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff + econ checks (tokens/$, prefetch, batching) — compact assumptions

Liam / team — sharing the concise assumption set we'll use for the MAP econ table. This is intentionally conservative for procurement review; we include an optimistic column for your internal planning.

Assumptions (per inference / averaged):
- average input tokens: 120 (user prompt + system + metadata)
- average output tokens: 80
- total tokens per call (A): 200
- baseline batching: 1 (no batch) 
- expected batching factor during pilot (B): 1.8 (we expect continuous batching at peak bursts with 10–50ms hold times)
- effective tokens per served inference with batching (A/B): ~111
- KV/prefix cache hit rate (C): 22% (saves repeated prompt tokens)
- tokens after cache (D): 111 * (1 - C) = ~87

Cost assumptions (hosted SKU example):
- price per 1M tokens (model-vX-q8): $35 (conservative tier)
- tokens-per-dollar (conservative) = 1,000,000 / 35 ≈ 28,571 tokens/$
- effective tokens per inference (D) ≈ 87 -> cost per inference ≈ 87 / 28,571 ≈ $0.00305
- tokens-per-dollar (optimistic pricing / better quant) = 40,000 tokens/$ -> cost per inference ≈ 87 / 40,000 ≈ $0.00218

Quick sensitivity (pilot scale sample):
- 50k DAU, 1 inference per active user per day (conservative): 50k inferences/day -> daily cost ≈ $153 (conservative) -> ~$4,590/month
- If average inferences/user/day = 2 -> monthly ≈ $9k (conservative)

Notes / risks:
- If we increase batching aggressively (factor >4) we see token efficiency gains but latency risk. We will preserve p50 SLA by capping hold times and prioritizing low-latency lanes for interactive flows.
- Prefetch (client-side + server-side) can improve effective cache hit rates; we can model a +15–30% improvement in C depending on session reuse.

Attachments referenced: I uploaded a short sim (prefetch-sim-results.csv) with a few run variants. Ben/Hannah — please add procurement notes / SOW bullets on the MAP when you see the draft.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

2) Please include a short SOW bullet that the pilot will not exceed p50 250ms for interactive endpoints; procurement wants that explicitly.

We can take the MAP + one-row econ summary to our legal/procurement review on 12/07 if we get the MAP and summary this week. I confirmed Wed 12/03 10:00am PT works — see the DocuSign placeholder in the related links; we'll be ready to lock the SOW once procurement signs off.

Thanks again — talk soon.
Liam
